exercise.name: Dumbbell Alternate Side Press

reference.title: Dumbbell Alternate Side Press
reference.listing: Page could not be read (blocked by the network proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.laterality: Alternating (right then left in one loop)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as each dumbbell presses up, inhale as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: Per side about 1.3 s up, 0.4 s at the top, 1.5 s down

prescription.load: Light to moderate dumbbells: the side bend loads the spine, so pick a weight you can press for the target reps with 2-3 reps in reserve (RIR 2-3) and full control.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then a slightly heavier pair; keep the lean smooth and controlled.

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip width, dumbbells in front of the shoulders at chin height, palms facing you, elbows down in front.
Breathe out and press one dumbbell up, turning the palm forward and letting the elbow open to the side, while you bend sideways at the waist away from it.
Arm straight overhead, reaching up and over toward the opposite side; ribs and hips stay facing forward.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell back to the shoulder as you straighten up, palm turning back toward you.
Both dumbbells at the shoulders, trunk upright; press the other side.

mistakes.fix: Keep the chest and hips facing forward; the trunk bends straight to the side.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back and arching the lower back
mistakes.fix: Brace the abs and keep the ribs down.

mistakes.mistake: Bending too far with a heavy weight
mistakes.fix: Keep the side bend moderate (about 10-20 degrees) and the weight light.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing in front of the face
mistakes.fix: Finish with the arm straight overhead, not out in front.
Hold it in front of the shoulder while the other arm works.

kinematics.norm: Moderate side bend away from the pressing arm, about 10-20 degrees (clinical opinion; bodybuilding.com see-saw press)

kinematics.setup: ≈147°, dumbbells in front of the shoulders, palms facing you
kinematics.norm: Elbow fully bent at the start, nearly straight at the top (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Pressing arm ≈16° from vertical, reaching over toward the opposite side
kinematics.norm: Arm straight overhead, reaching toward the opposite side (bodybuilding.com see-saw press)

kinematics.peak: Palm forward at the top (forearm turn 2° plus upper-arm rotation)
kinematics.norm: Palms facing you at the start, palm forward at the top, as in the Arnold press (bodybuilding.com see-saw press)

kinematics.peak: Holds its dumbbell in front of the shoulder
kinematics.norm: Holds its dumbbell at the shoulder (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Per side 1.3 s up, 0.4 s at the top, 1.5 s down
kinematics.norm: About 1-1.5 s up, 1.5-2 s down per side (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #1352, Dumbbell Alternate Side Press, video (movement reference; page not readable here)
Bodybuilding.com, see-saw press (alternating side press): press one dumbbell overhead, rotating the palm forward, while bending at the hip toward the opposite side
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2013, effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses (J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)

cautions: Use light weights: a heavy load combined with a side bend can strain the lower back (bodybuilding.com see-saw press).
Shoulder pain overhead: reduce the range or press without the side bend.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Lower back discomfort: press without the side bend (standing alternating dumbbell press).
regressions: Dumbbell Arnold press without the lean.
progressions: Pause 2 s at the top of each press.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Raises the arm forward and up from the Arnold start (Campos 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: As the right side, half a cycle later.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Takes over as the elbow opens out to the side and the arm goes overhead.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbow at the top.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Rotate the shoulder blade up as the arm goes overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blade upward with the trapezius.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Control the side bend; the obliques on the side being lengthened brake the lean (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Bend the trunk toward the left as the right arm presses.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the spine steady; standing one-arm dumbbell pressing raised trunk muscle activity (Saeterbakken 2012; 2013).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level as the trunk leans.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level as the trunk leans.

guides.label: Press up and over as the trunk bends away
